pieces.name: Conformance to the MACE reference implementation
pieces.judge: Does SimpleAtom use MACE the way upstream says to? Where it differs, is the difference deliberate and documented, or a bug?
pieces.gap: modelType has no allow-list: custom with no uploaded model silently returns MACE-MP-0 results labelled custom, shareable and PDF-exportable. Plus non-converged optimisations reported as completed, dtype inverted vs upstream, and MD potential energy labelled total energy.

notes: Scope is MACE-only. No orbitals, partial charges, Fukui indices, pKa, docking, or DFT — MACE is an interatomic potential with no electron density.
Rowan's typeface Matter is commercially licensed and is not used. SimpleAtom keeps Fraunces + Inter.
Viewer pieces share one file and are serialised, not run in parallel.
Audit found results-display.tsx is dead code; metrics-dashboard.tsx is the live results component.
Audit found FIRE optimizer advertised in docs and landing copy, but BFGS is hardcoded in mace-api/calculate.py. Being corrected.
Of Rowan's ~30 workflows: 2 already shipped, 18 buildable on MACE, 13 blocked by the absence of any electron-density model.
Measured: both our viewer and Rowan render at exactly devicePixelRatio 2.00. The original DPR-1 premise was wrong — 3Dmol upscales by default when antialias is on.
Blind label-stripping was not achievable for the qualitative comparison; critics run with fresh context and an adversarial brief instead. Stated rather than claimed otherwise.
Critic measured Rowan as having NO specular term either (brightest pixel 242/255, zero >=245). The 3Dmol fork is rejected on measurement, not deferred.
Critic found our shading objectively beats the bar (117 luminance levels on carbon vs 34; we run SSAO, Rowan has none). We lost purely on scale.

CIF fractional coordinates were never converted through the unit cell. Silicon loaded with nearest-neighbour 0.433 A instead of 2.3516 A — a factor of 5.4. Fixed and covered by public/demo/silicon.cif.

Four separate defects in this branch were code that reviews as correct and does nothing at runtime: the validator dead bounds, the phonon fallthrough, the no-op D3 toggle, and the inert structure guardrails.
Two agents (viewer round-2 critic, guardrail wiring) died on a session limit. The wiring was completed directly; the critic re-run is still outstanding.

ACEsuit/mace audit: the float64-for-Hessians rule in CLAUDE.md is not sourced from upstream and targets phonon, which SimpleAtom rejects, so it guards nothing. Upstream says use float64 for geometry optimisation, a feature SimpleAtom has.
Fifth instance of the silent-fallthrough pattern: modelType joins calculationType, the validator bounds, the D3 toggle and the structure guardrails.

CORRECTION: the claim that our shading beats the bar does not replicate. AO was never enabled (renderer._AOEnabled === false) and carbon tonality measures 237 distinct luminance levels for both viewers, not 117 vs 34.
Round-2 critic verdicts: viewer ROWAN, landing ROWAN, nav ROWAN. Three losses, all with specific measured causes.
v2.1 continues the loop from main. Viewer, landing and nav all have their round-N fixes shipped and are awaiting re-judgment.

FIRST WIN: nav. Critic measured Rowan uses the same mx-auto max-w-7xl px-6 with logo at x=24 and h1 at x=144.5 — a 120.5px offset against our 121px. Full-bleed chrome over a narrower column is the bar own pattern, not a defect.

SETTLED by ablation: ambient occlusion is genuinely active. Disabling it changes 14,024 of 103,106 pixels, all strictly interior to the silhouette. The 117-vs-34 luminance claim is dead — 241 with AO on, 241 with AO off; that metric never measured shading.
The transparency fix alone was a pixel-level no-op: the well behind the canvas painted the identical white the opaque canvas had painted. Removing the well is what makes it mean anything.

Provenance: the checkpoint is identified by watching torch.load rather than re-deriving upstream cache paths, which would go stale silently. e3nn loads its own constants.pt in the same window, so selection is by explicit rule and the rule that fired is recorded.

validate_calculation.py called logging.disable(CRITICAL) at MODULE scope. Importing it would have silently re-broken MACE warning capture process-wide and permanently in the FastAPI server. Moved into a CLI-only helper, with a regression test.

Framing root cause: maxDrawnRadius() added the largest radius of ANY element present to the extreme projected coordinate, estimating max|x-c| + max r where the truth is max(|x-c| + r). The error scales with radii, so bulkier representations over-padded and under-zoomed more — that was the spacefill inversion.

defectsFixed.what: modelType had no allow-list — selecting a custom model with no checkpoint returned MACE-MP-0 results labelled custom, shareable and PDF-exportable
calculationType had no allow-list — any unrecognised type (incl. phonon) silently ran a single-point and returned it as the requested calculation
CIF fractional coordinates were never converted through the unit cell — silicon loaded with nearest-neighbour 0.433 A instead of 2.3516 A
The scientific validator has never run: the documented path does not exist, and its model-aware energy bounds were dead code
BFGS convergence was discarded — an optimisation that exhausted maxOptSteps was reported as completed
MD recorded potential energy but called it total energy and told users to check NVE conservation — impossible, KE was never recorded
MACE-OFF forced to float32, inverting upstream default_dtype=float64, with the downcast warning suppressed
MD was unreproducible — velocities and thermostat both drew from global np.random
Docs and landing copy advertised a FIRE optimizer that does not exist; BFGS is hardcoded
D3 toggle was live but a silent no-op for custom models, whose loader takes no dispersion argument
npm run lint reported 42,891 problems from a linted virtualenv, making the no-new-warnings gate meaningless
result.params reported requested rather than effective values for dispersion and precision
